Synagogue in Siena

Synagogue · Siena, Italy

The Siena Synagogue is one of Tuscany’s most remarkable historic synagogues and a lasting monument to the city’s Jewish community. Built in 1786 in the heart of Siena’s former Jewish Ghetto, the synagogue is hidden behind a restrained exterior, reflecting the restrictions once imposed on Jewish worship. Inside, the sanctuary opens into an elegant and richly decorated space combining Rococo and Neoclassical elements, with a finely carved wooden ark, historic furnishings, and a women’s gallery. The synagogue survived centuries of political change and remains an important witness to the long history of Jewish life in Siena.
